touch_interrupt.about: Touching a Brobot cuts its chat reply short - native Wire-Pod, on by default. A scripted song turns it off for its own run ("touch_interrupt_off": true in its knobs.json, the Bingo test): the song engine creates off_file in GOPOD's overlay chipper folder when a live run starts and deletes it when the run ends; kill-bingo-test deletes it too. While off_file exists, touch does not interrupt. The wake-word interrupt is never changed (operator 2026-10-01: "Touch interrupt ON/OFF to default ON again").

native_intent.about: 2026-10-18 (operator: "\"Who am I\" (Backpack to Brobot 1) show a generic silent system bubble: wire-pod intent activated"): a native Wire-Pod intent sent to a Brobot (his own answer - Wire-Pod doesn't know his words) shows text in a silent bubble of role, once per once_seconds (gopodNativeBubble, gopod_native.go). Not for Wire-Pod's system intents (no audio, unmatched).
native_intent.notice_about: 2026-10-21 (operator: "Same as message inside a brobot chat bubble: Easter Egg 'What GOPOD is' ... add similar Native wire-pod Intent Detected * Template it"): now a notice inside that Brobot's bubble - its words are bubble_notices.native_intent; typed cube commands too. role and text are no longer used.

gopod_yourself.about: The wake phrase in the Brobots layer (operator 2026-10-09: "GOPOD Yourself > GOPOD layer (isn't built yet) ... tie in to brobot 1 CTA > newsletter ... brobot 2 CTA > crushn8r.ca"; gopod_yourself.go). A typed, numpad or spoken line that is one of phrases (after "hey vector" or a Brobot's name) gets that Brobot's line here; to both Brobots, Brobot 1 then Brobot 2. The GOPOD_YOURSELF voice command hands a spoken one to the chat for both, and the same phrase again within repeat_seconds (the other robot heard it too) is dropped. A question about it ("what is GOPOD Yourself?") still goes to the chat. When the GOPOD layer is built, the phrase points there instead.

lines.Brobot 1: Join the CRUSHN8R CREW'd newsletter. You're joining the crew, not a list!

song_stop.about: Stopping a song run at the next safe spot (operator 2026-10-04: "stop the current run at the next safe spot"; 2026-10-09: "add 'stop run' as an input command for songs/runs"). A typed or numpad stop_words line, or a "thanks Brobots", runs safe_script when engine is running (a song): it creates request_file in GOPOD's overlay chipper folder, and the song engine checks it before each step and ends the run there the normal way (control handed back, touch interrupt on). If the run hasn't ended after wait_seconds, it force-stops it like the kill-bingo-test alias. stop_words stops a playing draft too (gopod_thanks_close_out.go). The KILL_BINGO_TEST voice command was cleared 2026-10-09.

native.about: Wire-Pod's own (native) voice answers - "Hey Vector, what time is it", the weather, volume and the rest of Wire-Pod's intent list (operator 2026-10-10: "Native “Hey Vector” answers during a run ... Native?[] makes this optional ... Change Wire-Pod's code if need be"; gopod_native.go, plus a gate in Wire-Pod's own matchIntentSend.go). The chat page's Native? box turns them on or off for the session; on_at_start is the state at Wire-Pod's start. During a run they are always off (session: a run owns the Brobots). Off: a phrase that matches a native intent gets Wire-Pod's quiet ending instead. GOPOD's voice commands and chat questions are not native and always get through. always_on: native intents that answer even when off (Wire-Pod intent names, e.g. intent_imperative_volumelevel_extend).
native.to_manager_about: 2026-10-21 (operator: "weather goes to PLAYHEAD instead"): a native intent here goes to the chat instead of Wire-Pod's own answer, and its manager take (managers.takes kind) takes it - spoken weather goes to PLAYHEAD, the same as a typed one. 2026-10-22 (operator: yes to "what time is it" to PLAYHEAD too): the clock too.

mic_service.about: One process owns the Jetson's USB room mic for both Record Session's master and the numpad push-to-talk (the mic can only be opened once). Started by Wire-Pod on first use, as the desktop user. It reuses the golden "Is That You" PTT writer's mic pick, timings, 48 kHz / 16 kHz resample and Vosk model (gopod_mic_service_001.py).

Other keys show their assigned persona. exit_taps taps of 000 (KP0) or of NumLock within exit_window_seconds turn it off (the Numpad? box unticks). 2026-10-08: on only while the Numpad? box on the typing line is ticked (operator: "a checked Numpad box indicates takeover of the usb keyboard numpad mapping"). Only while the chat window is open. Before LLM Ready a key records nothing and shows not_ready (operator 2026-10-09: "LLM not ready? Too bad!! Wait!!"). The status texts show in grey Goverlord system bubbles; {key} {brobot} {persona} {body} {min} {error} {how} are filled in. 2026-10-09 (operator: "upon numpad checked, I cannot type normally * I have a keyboard + numpad in one"): while a text box has the focus, every key types as usual. 2026-10-10 (live: "numpad checkbox didn't work" after typing): with Numpad? ticked, the numpad's own keys are always push-to-talk, even in a text box; every other key types. Esc still leaves the box.

record_session.about: Record Session (operator 2026-10-04, gopod_notes/RECORD_SESSION_SPEC_003.md): the box on the chat window's typed-input line. Ticked: recording starts at the next safe point (no Brobot reply in progress) into sessions_dir/<date>/<time><folder_suffix>/ - the Jetson USB room mic (through mic_service, the golden PTT writer's mic pick, 48 kHz master), every chat line (chat.jsonl), every Wire-Pod log line (wirepod.log), and chat.html at stop. Unticked: stops, zips the folder, keeps the zip, deletes the loose files. "Thanks Brobots" while recording, or max_minutes reached: stops, then ask_brobot asks; a typed or spoken line with all keep_words keeps (zip), with all delete_words deletes; no answer in answer_wait_minutes deletes. The answer shows as Operator to answer_to; confirm_brobot says kept_text or deleted_text and the box unticks. A Wire-Pod restart deletes a folder still waiting for an answer and zips one that was cut off mid-recording.
record_session.ask_text: Session over. Keep the session recording, or delete the session recording?
record_session.take_sheet_about: Keep also adds the session's answers to the take sheet as takes (operator 2026-10-06: "keep this session take?"), one per Brobot answer, filed under the value points it was given; delete adds nothing. Empty: no takes.

battery_watch.about: The battery watchdog (operator 2026-10-15: "set up a background watchdog to monitor battery level over time? Over the course of a session run? If let's say the battery level drops below a threshold (like from a lot of use), have the brobot comment they're feeling dizzy and need help getting home, lol"; gopod_battery_watch.go). For the whole Wire-Pod session, every interval_seconds each Brobot's battery is read and logged (GOPOD_BATTERY_WATCH). Below low_volts, off the charger, he says one of his lines with his bubble - once; again only after he's back up to recover_volts or set on his charger. Never in the middle of a reply or a run: he waits until both are over. low_volts: golden rule 6's line, 3.7 V (Brobot 2's crashes came at 3.61-3.62 V). The lines are drafts in the operator's words, to edit.

Brobot 1: Whoa, bro... I'm feeling dizzy. I need help getting home.
Brobot 2: Bro, I'm feeling dizzy... can someone help me get home?

reporter_voices.about: The reporter voices, heard through the chat page (operator 2026-10-06: "have the female/male voices speak operator bubble"; "since 1 operator, use female reporter voice (brobot 3)"; "can you channel the audio to play through the wire-pod web page?"). hosts: each reporter's Kokoro voice. A line typed on the page (read_lines_from: how Wire-Pod logs it) is read out first - a line to Brobot 1 by Reporter 1 (Brobot 3, female), to Brobot 2 by Reporter 2 (Brobot 4, male) (read_by; operator 2026-10-06), a line to both by operator_host, then the Brobot answers (waiting its length plus page_lag_seconds, at most max_wait_seconds). labels: each host bubble's header (operator 2026-10-06: "Reporter 1, Brobot 3:" / "Reporter 2, Brobot 4:"). opening: queued once the LLM is warm and the opening's voice files are made (at most start_wait_seconds), followed by an opening_end_text line. The page plays nothing until its Log section is open and has been clicked (operator 2026-10-06: "pause the chat bubbles from running until its clicked to and viewable"); it then plays what's queued, one voice line after another, and tells Wire-Pod when the opening is heard. Only then is it LLM Ready, and the warm-up gate opens: until then a typed, numpad or voice question to a Brobot is dropped (logged GOPOD_WARMUP_GATE). With no page, the gate opens after gate_max_seconds; closing: after "Thanks Brobots", in the ending's order (sign_off.about; ALIAS-PLAY-STUDIO.md "The thanks ending") - the interview vamp's own lines, word for word (02a_brobots_interview_vamp/story.md, m1_c-m1_g and m4_c-m4_e), shown as host bubbles. Every line is made once into a WAV in webroot/audio_folder by the worker (one Kokoro load at Wire-Pod start, about 25 s) and kept there: the bookends are pre-generated at start, and a line said before is never made again. The page can only play sound after it has been clicked or typed in once. Needs wpr 2. say_words: the reporter's word replacements, said instead of the word (whole words, any case; operator 2026-10-06: "reporter word replacements - start a list ... thx = thanks") - the bubble keeps what was typed. gap_seconds: the page's pause between two voice lines.

reporter_voices.finish_wait_seconds_about: 2026-10-20 (operator: "add a 'wait until I'm finished' flag to the chat bubble template"; live: a long Operator voice was still playing when the flat 30 s cap ran out and GOPOD went on): every voiced line waits until the page has played it (heard) - its own length plus up to this many seconds for the page's queue; 0 = the old cap (2 x max_wait_seconds).
reporter_voices.heard_margin_seconds_about: 2026-10-14 (operator: "make GOPOD respond the lines' own length plus a few seconds * no more estimates of time padding please, or as minimal as needed * more responsive so I know what I can control"): a line Wire-Pod waits on goes on the moment the page says it has played it (the heard check); with no answer, after the queued lines' own lengths plus this many seconds (never more than 2 x max_wait_seconds). page_lag_seconds is no longer added to a wait.
reporter_voices.generating_about: 2026-10-14 (operator: "when this happens during a live run * rule: Display 'generating...' during the lag time * upon voice generated, update to message and play"): a line shown with its voice whose voice file isn't made yet first shows a grey Goverlord bubble with generating_text; once the voice is made, a Goverlord line fills that bubble and plays, any other line takes its place.
reporter_voices.generating_text_about: 2026-10-16 (operator: "update message to 'Voice file generating.' + hourglass * update message upon voice wav play"): the grey bubble, with the warm-up's hourglass, while a line's voice file is made; the line takes its place when its voice plays.

opening.text: Okay. We're about to go live. Our News Crew is ready. Grab the mic or grab the umbrella, I don't care which, just don't drop either one.
I've got the mic AND the umbrella. I'm doing both jobs. I am a professional.
Good. You're doing one job. I'm doing the other job. That's the whole system. That's why it works.
Correct. The system works. Two hosts, one mission: get you people hyped before two Brobots who used to be considered trash, have an actual conversation.
Okay. Rescued. The point is, something is being prepared right now, live, as we speak. And we are going to be here, to make it feel like an epic event. Because it is, truly an event of a lifetime.
And its our job to make it happen. I'm so excited. Do you feel that?
My hands are full. I am a professional.
That is not nerves. That is anticipation.

closing.text: It's going to be great. Go on and GOPOD Yourself. Find out what's all about.
Umbrella's down. Umbrella was never really necessary, there was never any rain.
The umbrella represents preparedness. Show is over.

sign_off.about: The ending after "thanks Brobots" (operator 2026-10-08: "New ending: 1/5/2/3/4/Operator bubble"): the sign-off, the reporters' closing, these lines, Record Session's keep-or-delete question, then system_text in a Goverlord system bubble (system_role) when a draft played, and last welcome_text, always (operator 2026-10-09: "thx bros is its own process ending with your welcome"). A "thanks" first closes out a playing draft or a running song at its next safe spot (gopod_thanks_close_out.go). Once per ending. A Brobot's line is said by the robot with a bubble; a reporter's (Brobot 3/4) through the page.

lines.text: This is where Pip asks for an email, right?

sign_off.nothing_recorded_text_about: 2026-10-24 (operator: "Yes, a line like 'Nothing recorded. You're welcome.'"): said before welcome_text when nothing was recorded this session (a recording says its kept/deleted line instead).
sign_off.safe_spot_seconds_about: 2026-10-16 (operator: "thanks guys anywhere in a line ends the session, at the next best safe spot"): the thanks ending waits this long, then until no Brobot is answering (to All: Brobot 2's sign-off first).

native_cube.about: Typed and numpad cube commands run the robot's own native cube behavior, as a spoken one does (operator 2026-10-08: "backpack vocal cube command should respond as native 'cube' command by default"; gopod_native_cube.go). A line holding one of these phrases is sent to the chosen Brobot as the intent (to All: both); first match wins. Spoken lines are matched by Wire-Pod itself (intent-data/en-US.json), not this list. Needs wpr 2.

live_weather.about: The live weather a draft answer says where it has {weather} (operator 2026-10-08: the Awaken line, "a live real-time weather check here ... if online is detected"; gopod_live_weather.go). Ported from the golden Awaken weather (gopod_weather_fetch_001.py): one OpenWeatherMap fetch with Wire-Pod's own weather key, said with location and date, both units and both clocks, the robot's own first (his RobotSettings: Brobot 1 Celsius/24-hour, Brobot 2 Fahrenheit/12-hour). A fetch is reused for cache_seconds, so Brobot 2 checks the same reading. Offline, offline_text is said in place of {weather} (operator 2026-10-09); left empty, the sentence with {weather} is left out. 2026-10-14: the bubble shows ° (said "degrees") and the 24-hour time as military time, four digits: "1814 Hours Military Time" (military_label), said "eighteen fourteen hours military time"; a named province/state/country picks the place (Windsor Ontario, not Windsor England)
live_weather.follow_up_kit_line_about: 2026-10-15 (operator: "can you add in brobot 2 follow up, the link to the weather kit web page? * somewhere before the, hey that reminds me..."): Brobot 2's follow-up to a weather question (All) gets this line after his own words, before his 'Hey, that reminds me...'. The bubble shows the link; he says its words.
live_weather.follow_up_kit_line: Want to see every weather face Vector has? Check out the [GOPOD Weather Kit](/gopod_weather_kit.html).
live_weather.offline_text: It appears as though we're offline! Only thing left to do is step outside, then GOPOD Yourself!!
